notes.printed: Every view cell reads: d in points (challenger minus comparator), its 95% interval, and its reading by the pre-registered decision rule against that view's margin. Margin in every view except the 5-point view: −10 points; the 5-point view's margin: −5 points.

Stamped view labels, in the file's own words. 5-point margin: "secondary, 5-point margin"; cached re-pricing: "cached view (offline re-pricing)"; sign-flip p: "sensitivity (superiority, d = 0)" (a superiority check against no difference, not against the margin).

notes.formula: the stamped text, verbatim in quotation marks (a quotation mark inside it as a single one); the value every row of the table prints (the build refuses a column that is not constant)
notes.printed: Refusals out and truncations out, as stamped: "no missing items in the five tests' arms" (the file's "arms" are this paper's settings). Tests 4 and 5 have no vote size k, so no k is shown for them in the cached re-pricing view. In the equal-token view k is 1 for every vote (Tests 1–3), so it is given here and is not a column.
raw: no missing items in the five tests' arms

notes.printed: Label of each column. As deployed: the confirmatory reading (as in TAB-02). Final answer and copy slips forgiven: pre-registered secondary views. Refusals out, truncations out and ties as wrong: pre-registered sensitivity checks. Original marking rule: the sensitivity check Deviation 2 fixed in Lock 3, before any main-run data (not a pre-registered secondary view). 5-point margin, cached re-pricing and equal-token view: reporting views fixed after Lock 3, before any result was opened. Superiority sign-flip p: a pre-specified sensitivity check against no difference. None of these views is a test.

What each view changes. Refusals out and truncations out: blocked or truncated calls are left out instead of counted wrong. Final answer: a sample is marked, and the vote counted, by its final answer only, not its step lines. Copy slips forgiven: a sample whose step lines differ from the key at one line only, with the next line right, counts as right. Ties as wrong: a vote whose top answers tie, the right one among them, scores nothing instead of an equal share. Cached re-pricing: the vote's repeated input is priced at cache rates, so the same money can buy a larger k. Equal-token view: k is the number of Haiku-medium samples whose mean total tokens fit within the comparator's (at least one), instead of its money.
Sonnet ran at medium effort, one level below its default, in Tests 3 and 5.
